evidence.reason: `recoverTornTail` reads the file into a UTF-8-decoded `string`, so `raw.lastIndexOf('\n')` returns a UTF-16 code-unit index. `fs.truncate` interprets `lastComplete + 1` as a byte length. If any preceding complete record contains non-ASCII characters (JSON.stringify does not escape them), the byte offset of the newline is larger than the character index, so recovery truncates before the newline and inside complete data. The next append then glues onto that fragment, producing a corrupt line that `load` rejects. The proposed Buffer-based byte search is the correct fix.
